mainTopic: A raped wife of a כהן and her כתובה; whether a wife who says "גרשתני" is believed (רב המנונא vs. רבא); the "השמים ביני לבינך" challenges; and the start of a story about a wife's revealing habit
overview: The גמרא finishes רבא's question about a כהן's wife who was raped. Does she lose her כתובה, or is it the husband's bad luck, like a man whose field was flooded? The answer comes from the משנה of "טמאה אני לך". The גמרא rules out every other case and shows the משנה must be about a raped wife of a כהן, and she collects her כתובה. Then a new question is raised: is a woman believed when she tells her husband "גרשתני"? רב המנונא says yes, because a woman would not lie to her husband's face about something he knows. רבא says no: "טמאה אני לך" was believed only because she would not shame herself, and a woman in a hard marriage may well be brazen. Each side is challenged from the wife's claim "השמים ביני לבינך", and each defends his own reasoning. The amud ends by beginning a story about a woman who brought her husband water to wash his hands on a night they had not been together. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The other side of רבא's question: the husband's bad luck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רבא's question. Maybe the loss belongs to the husband, like a man whose field was flooded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it is the man whose field was flooded, so she should get her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the second half of רבא's question about a כהן's wife who was raped and is now forbidden to him. It suggests that the problem is the husband's misfortune, so she should still collect her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a כהן is what forces him to send her away, since a raped woman stays permitted to an ordinary Jewish husband. So the "disaster" falls on him, like a flood hitting his own field, and he should pay. This sets up the question the גמרא is about to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: His field was flooded: a picture of bad luck that falls on a specific person

phrases.english: And it is the man whose field was flooded.
phrases.notes: Literally 'his field was flooded': it's his bad luck, since his being a כהן is what forbids her to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's two-sided question from before this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a raped wife of a כהן, who is now forbidden to him, collect her כתובה?

steps.title: The answer is in the משנה of "I am defiled to you"
steps.stepSummary: The answer to רבא is pointed out from a משנה: a woman who says "טמאה אני לך" gets her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We told him: this is our משנה. A woman who says "I am defiled to you" has a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer to רבא's question is said to be a משנה that already exists. That משנה says a woman who tells her husband "I am forbidden to you" still collects her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far this only quotes the משנה. The next steps prove that the משנה must be talking about exactly רבא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: "I am defiled to you": I have become forbidden to you
The marriage contract payment a wife receives at divorce

phrases.english: And we said to him: it is our משנה:
phrases.notes: "Him" means רבא, who asked the question.

phrases.english: A woman who says "I am defiled to you"
has a כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question by quoting a משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman who says "טמאה אני לך" collects her כתובה, which will be shown to be רבא's exact case.

steps.title: The משנה cannot be about an ordinary Jew's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which wife the משנה means. It rules out a ישראל's wife: if she was willing she gets no כתובה, and if she was forced she is not forbidden at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If it is an ordinary Jew's wife: if she was willing, does she get any כתובה? And if she was forced, is she forbidden to her husband?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to prove that the משנה matches רבא's case. It does this by ruling out the other possibilities, starting with an ordinary Jew's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary Jew's wife who sinned willingly loses her כתובה, so the משנה cannot mean her. If she was raped, she stays permitted to him, so there would be no divorce to discuss. Either way, a ישראל's wife does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
The wife of an ordinary Jew (not a כהן)

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing?
If we say with the wife of an ordinary Jew,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּרָצוֹן — כְּלוּם יֵשׁ לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה?
phrases.english: if it was willingly, does she have any כתובה?
And if it was by force,
is she forbidden to the man?
phrases.notes: No, she isn't. A ישראל's wife who was raped stays permitted to her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving that the quoted משנה fits רבא's case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of wife and which situation is the משנה describing?

steps.title: So it must be a raped wife of a כהן, and she gets her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A כהן's wife who was willing cannot be meant either, so the משנה must be about a raped wife of a כהן. The משנה says she has a כתובה, which answers רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a כהן's wife. If she was willing, does she get any כתובה? Is she any better than an ordinary Jew's wife who was willing? So it must be by force, and the משנה teaches she has a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out a willing כהן's wife too. The only case left is a כהן's wife who was raped, and the משנה says she gets her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A willing כהן's wife cannot be better off than a willing ישראל's wife, who loses her כתובה. That leaves only רבא's exact case, and the משנה gives her the כתובה. So the answer is: the husband's "field was flooded," and he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: Is she worse off / any less (strict)
Rather, is it not that...: introduces the only option left

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן's wife who was raped is forbidden to her husband, but she still collects her כתובה. The loss falls on him.

phrases.english: But rather, it is about a כהן's wife.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּרָצוֹן — כְּלוּם יֵשׁ לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה?
phrases.english: If it was willingly, does she have any כתובה?
Is she any less than an ordinary Jew's wife who was willing?
phrases.notes: The willing ישראל's wife loses her כתובה, so the כהן's wife surely does too.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not by force?
And it teaches: she has a כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes ruling out the other cases and lands on רבא's case
steps.raayaObject: A raped wife of a כהן collects her כתובה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of "טמאה אני לך", once every other case has been ruled out

steps.title: New question: a wife who says "You divorced me"
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if a wife tells her husband "you divorced me" and he denies it, is she believed?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if she said to her husband "You divorced me," what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks whether a woman is believed when she claims, to her husband's face, that he divorced her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband himself knows whether he divorced her, so she is making a claim he can deny from his own knowledge. The next two steps argue both ways using the משנה of "טמאה אני לך".

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If she said to her husband "You divorced me," what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, related to the same משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a wife believed when she claims her husband divorced her?

steps.title: רב המנונא: she is believed, since she would not lie to his face
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא argues that even the later משנה, which does not believe "טמאה אני לך", would believe "גרשתני". The husband knows the truth, and a woman will not brazenly lie to her husband's face.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: Come and hear the case of a woman who says "I am defiled to you." Even the later משנה, which says she is not believed, holds that only there does she lie, because she knows her husband doesn't know about it. But with "you divorced me," which he knows about, she is believed, because there is a חזקה that a woman will not be brazen in front of her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא tries to answer the question from the משנה of "טמאה אני לך". He argues that a wife who says "you divorced me" is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the later משנה, "טמאה אני לך" is not believed because the husband cannot check it, so she might lie. "גרשתני" is about something the husband knows firsthand. Lying to his face would take a brazenness that the חזקה says a wife does not have, so here she is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: The later version of the משנה (which stopped believing her)
A firm assumption about how people behave
Acts brazenly, lies to someone's face

steps.confusionAlert: There were two versions of the משנה. The first (משנה ראשונה) believed "טמאה אני לך"; the later one (משנה אחרונה) did not. רב המנונא builds his argument on the later, stricter one.

phrases.english: רב המנונא said: Come and hear:
A woman who says "I am defiled to you":
for even according to the later משנה
which teaches that she is not believed,
it is only there that she lies,
because she knows her husband doesn't know about her.
But with "you divorced me," which he knows about, she is believed,

phrases.aramaic: דַּחֲזָקָה אֵין אִשָּׁה מְעִיזָּה פָּנֶיהָ בִּפְנֵי בַּעְלָהּ.
phrases.english: because there is a חזקה that a woman will not be brazen in front of her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question in step 5
steps.raayaObject: A wife who says "גרשתני" is believed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of "טמאה אני לך", read according to the later version, plus the חזקה that a wife will not lie to her husband's face

steps.title: רבא: on the contrary, here she would be brazen
steps.stepSummary: רבא turns the argument upside down. Even the first משנה, which believes "טמאה אני לך", believes her only because a woman would not shame herself falsely. With "גרשתני", a woman unhappy with her husband may well be brazen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: On the contrary! Even the first משנה, which says she is believed, believes her there only because a woman does not shame herself. But here, where sometimes life with the man is hard for her, she would surely be brazen.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב המנונא's proof and argues the opposite: a woman who says "you divorced me" is not believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the reason the first משנה believed "טמאה אני לך" was that a woman would not falsely disgrace herself. That reason does not apply to "גרשתני", which brings her no shame. If she wants out of a hard marriage, she might lie boldly even to her husband's face, so the חזקה does not help here.

keyTerms.meaning: The first version of the משנה (which believed her)

steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא: "גרשתני" is believed, because a woman won't lie to her husband's face. רבא: it is not believed, because the only reason "טמאה אני לך" was ever believed is that she wouldn't shame herself, and a woman in a hard marriage may be brazen.

phrases.english: רבא said to him: On the contrary,
even according to the first משנה
which teaches that she is believed,

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא עֲבִידָא לְבַזּוֹיֵי נַפְשַׁהּ,
phrases.english: there it is because she would not disgrace herself,
but here, where sometimes
it is hard for her with the man,
she would surely be brazen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב המנונא's proof and argues the reverse
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both רב המנונא's comparison and his conclusion that "גרשתני" is believed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reason for believing "טמאה אני לך" was that she would not shame herself, which does not apply to "גרשתני". A woman in a hard marriage may be brazen to her husband's face.

steps.title: רב משרשיא challenges רבא from the earlier משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא points out that in the earlier version of the משנה, a woman who says "השמים ביני לבינך" is believed, even though that claim does not embarrass her. This seems to disprove רבא's idea that she is believed only because she would not shame herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא objected: The case of "Heaven is between me and you" in the first version of the משנה should disprove רבא. Here she has nothing to be embarrassed about, and still the משנה teaches that she is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא attacks רבא's reasoning from Step 7 using a case from the same earlier version of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the earlier משנה believed "טמאה אני לך" only because a woman would not falsely shame herself. But "השמים ביני לבינך" sounds like a polite, general claim with no shame in it. Even so, the earlier משנה believed her. That suggests shame was never the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: the earlier version of the משנה, before the ruling was changed
"Heaven is between me and you": the wife's claim about a private marital problem

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya raised an objection:
"Heaven is between me and you" of the first version of the משנה
phrases.notes: This is another of the wife's claims in our משנה: only Heaven knows the private problem between them.

phrases.english: is a refutation of רבא,
for here she has no embarrassment,
and yet it teaches that she is believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's rejection of רב המנונא from Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the earlier משנה believed the woman only because of shame
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "השמים ביני לבינך" involves no shame, yet the earlier משנה believed her, so shame cannot be the reason she is believed.

steps.title: רבא answers: she must spell out an embarrassing detail
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that "השמים ביני לבינך" is embarrassing after all. To make the claim, she has to say openly that "אין יורה כחץ", and she would not say something like that unless it were true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא holds: There, since it is not enough for her unless she says "he does not shoot like an arrow," if it were not as she says, she would not say it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself. He shows that the "Heaven" claim really does involve shame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The polite phrase alone is not enough to win her case. She has to explain the intimate detail that her husband is "אין יורה כחץ". Saying that out loud is shameful, so the same shame logic still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not enough for her
"shoots like an arrow": normal, forceful emission of seed, needed for having children

phrases.english: רבא holds:
there, since it is not enough for her
unless she says "he does not shoot like an arrow,"
if it were not as she says,
she would not say it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the claim does involve shame
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "השמים ביני לבינך" is just a vague, polite claim with no embarrassment
steps.terutzMaskana: She has to state the embarrassing detail "אין יורה כחץ", so shame is still why she is believed

steps.title: The later משנה seems to challenge רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: In the later version of the משנה, a woman who says "השמים ביני לבינך" is not believed, even though her husband knows the truth just as she does. This seems to disprove רב המנונא, who said she is believed when the husband knows the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Heaven is between me and you" in the later version of the משנה should disprove רב המנונא. Here she knows, and her husband knows about her, and still the משנה teaches that she is not believed!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to the other side and challenges רב המנונא from the later version of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא said in Step 6 that "גרשתני" is believed because the husband knows the truth, so she would not dare lie to his face. In the "Heaven" case both of them also seem to know the truth. Yet the later משנה does not believe her.

keyTerms.meaning: the later version of the משנה, after the ruling was changed

phrases.english: "Heaven is between me and you" of the later version of the משנה
should be a refutation of רב המנונא:
for here she knows,
and her husband knows about her,
and yet it teaches that she is not believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רבא to challenging רב המנונא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's view that a woman is believed when her husband knows the truth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the "Heaven" case the husband also knows, yet the later משנה does not believe her.

steps.title: רב המנונא answers: she thinks he cannot know this detail
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא explains that in the "Heaven" case the woman tells herself that her husband knows whether they were intimate, but not whether he is "יורה כחץ". Because she thinks he cannot contradict her, she is willing to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא holds: Here too, she says to herself: Granted, he knows about the intercourse, but does he know about shooting like an arrow? Because of this she may lie.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא defends his view by showing that the "Heaven" case is different from "גרשתני".
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule depends on the husband truly knowing the fact in question. A husband certainly knows whether he gave a divorce. But the woman assumes he does not know about "יורה כחץ", so she does not feel she is lying to his face.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side keeps its own reasoning. רבא: a woman is believed when the claim shames her. רב המנונא: a woman is believed when the husband truly knows the fact, and in the "Heaven" case she thinks he does not know it.

phrases.english: רב המנונא holds:
here too, she herself says:
phrases.notes: She is saying this to herself, in her heart, not out loud.

phrases.english: granted that about the intercourse he knows,
about shooting like an arrow, does he know?
And because of this she lies.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the husband does not really know the detail in question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the "Heaven" case the husband knows the truth just like in "גרשתני"
steps.terutzMaskana: She believes he cannot know about "יורה כחץ", so she may lie; with a divorce he surely knows

steps.title: A story about a woman who brought water to wash her husband's hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about a woman whose habit was to wash her husband's hands each morning after they had been intimate. One day she brought water when they had not been together. When he pointed this out, she began to answer, and the story continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain woman who, every day after intimacy, would get up early and wash her husband's hands. One day she brought him water to wash. He said to her: "This thing did not happen just now!" She said to him: "If so, one of the gentiles..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story that is connected to the theme of a wife's claims. It is setting up a case that continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her washing his hands was a known sign that they had been intimate that night. By bringing water on a night when nothing happened, she seemed to reveal that someone else had been with her. Her answer hints at this, and the rest comes in the next section.

phrases.english: There was a certain woman
who on every day of intimacy
would rise early and wash her husband's hands.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד אַתְיָא לֵיהּ מַיָּא לְמִמְשֵׁא.
phrases.english: One day she brought him water to wash.
He said to her:
This thing did not happen now!
phrases.notes: He means they weren't intimate last night, so why bring the water?

phrases.english: She said to him: If so,
one of the gentiles

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theoretical debate to a real-life story about a wife's claim
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: a woman's habit revealed something her husband knew had not happened; the outcome continues in the next section
